label: Accordion
summary: A vertically stacked set of expansion panels.
overview:
The accordion is one tab stop: the Up and Down arrow keys move focus between the panel headers, Home and End jump to the first and last. Disabled panels are skipped. Without multiple, opening a panel (by the person or by setting open) closes the others.

Items fire open and close; the older accordion-item-toggle event still fires but is deprecated.
example: ```html Panel 1 Summary text Content Panel 2 Content ```

attributes.name: multiple
attributes.description:
Whether multiple panels can be expanded simultaneously.
When `false` (default), expanding one panel collapses all others.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description:
Variant for the accordion.
`'default'` renders panels with a subtle background on expand and dividers between items.
`'flat'` renders panels without borders or background changes — suitable for use inside cards.

attributes.name: leading-toggle
attributes.description:
When `true`, the toggle icon is placed at the leading start of the header.
When `false` (default), the icon is placed at the trailing end.

label: Alert
summary: Alerts show short, prominent contextual messages in the page, with an optional icon, action and close button.
overview:
An alert is part of the page. For a transient message use wc-snackbar, or wc-notification-manager for a queue of them.

An alert is not a live region by default, so an alert that is on the page when it loads is read in the normal reading order and not announced. Set live="polite" (status) or live="assertive" (alert) on an alert you add or change while the page is in use.

With dismissible a close button fires a cancelable close event with reason: 'action' and then hides the alert (sets hidden). Call preventDefault() on the event to keep it, for example to remove it yourself.
slot: action - Buttons at the end of the alert, for example `<wc-button variant="text" size="sm">`.
fires: close - Fired, cancelable, when the close button is pressed. The alert hides unless the event is cancelled.
cssprop: --alert-border-radius - Border radius of the alert surface.
example:
```html
<wc-alert intent="warning" dismissible description="Your trial ends in 3 days.">
  <wc-button slot="action" variant="text" size="sm">Upgrade</wc-button>
</wc-alert>
```

label: App Bar
summary: A top app bar for page-level navigation and actions.
overview:
The app bar component implements the top app bar pattern. It provides a consistent header for screens, housing a navigation icon, a page title/headline, and optional trailing action icons.

Four size variants are available: small (64dp, single-row), center-aligned (64dp, centred headline), medium (112dp, headline below the row), and large (152dp, large headline).

Use the start slot for a navigation icon (e.g. a hamburger or back button), the default slot for the headline text, and the end slot for action icon buttons.

The app bar is not a landmark on its own, so it can sit in cards, panes and dialogs. For the page's banner, put it in a <header> element.

The leading and trailing slots are deprecated aliases of start and end and are removed in 4.0.
slot: trailing - Deprecated: use `end`.
cssprop: --app-bar-shadow - Box-shadow applied when the bar is scrolled / elevated.
example:
```html
<!-- Large app bar -->
<wc-app-bar variant="large">
  <wc-icon-button slot="start" variant="text"><wc-icon name="arrow_back"></wc-icon></wc-icon-button>
  Large Headline
  <wc-icon-button slot="end" variant="text"><wc-icon name="more_vert"></wc-icon></wc-icon-button>
</wc-app-bar>
```

label: Avatar
summary: The Avatar component is used to represent user, and displays the profile picture, initials or fallback icon.
overview:
The avatar shows the image at src. Without one, or when the image fails to load, it shows the initials of name (the first letters of its first and last words), and without a name a person icon.

The avatar is named by label, or else name: the image gets it as alt, the initials and the icon as role="img" with aria-label. An avatar with neither is decorative and hidden from assistive technology.

size (sm, md, lg) sets --avatar-size; setting the custom property directly still wins.

example:
```html

<wc-avatar name="Grace Brewster Hopper"></wc-avatar>
```

label: Badge
summary: The badge component is used to display a small amount of information to the user.
overview:
A badge shows a count, or with dot (or no value) a small dot. A number above max (default 99) shows as 99+.

A dot alone means nothing to a screen reader, so it is hidden from assistive technology unless it has a label. Give a count a label such as "3 unread messages" when the number alone is not enough. When the badge sits on an icon button, put the full meaning in the button's aria-label instead (for example "Inbox, 3 unread") and leave the badge without a label.

intent (info, success, warning, danger) sets its color; without it the badge uses the theme's badge color.
cssprop: --badge-text-color - Controls the color of the count.
example:
```html
<wc-badge value="1"></wc-badge>
<wc-badge value="120" label="120 unread messages"></wc-badge>
<wc-badge dot intent="success"></wc-badge>
```

label: Bottom Sheet
summary: Bottom sheets slide up from the bottom of the screen to reveal additional content. Supports standard and modal variants.
overview:
The sheet renders a native <dialog>. The modal variant (the default) opens it with showModal(): it renders in the browser's top layer above the page, with a scrim; the rest of the page is inert and does not scroll; focus moves to the first element with autofocus inside it and returns where it was when the sheet closes. Escape and a click on the scrim close it (no-light-dismiss keeps it open on scrim clicks).

The drag handle closes the sheet when dragged down, clicked, or pressed with Enter or Space.

The standard variant opens the dialog with show(): it is not modal and stays in the page flow at the end of its container.

overview:

 - They help users understand their current location within the site hierarchy.
 - Follows WCAG 2.1 guidelines for accessible navigation landmarks.

label: Button
summary: Buttons help people initiate actions, from sending an email, to sharing a document, to liking a post.
overview:
Buttons are clickable elements that are used to trigger actions. They communicate calls to action to the user and allow users to interact with pages in a variety of ways. Button labels express what action will occur when the user interacts with it.

level is a preset of color and variant: primary (primary, filled), secondary (surface, tonal), tertiary (primary, text) and danger (danger, filled). A color or variant you set wins over it.

Set toggle to make a toggle button: it renders aria-pressed, flips selected on each click and fires change. selected does nothing without toggle.

label: Code Editor
summary: A Monaco-based code editing component with syntax highlighting, completions and debugging marks.
overview:
- CodeEditor wraps Monaco Editor as a web component, in the same frame as `wc-code-highlighter`: an optional header with a title and actions, or a copy button that floats at the top end. Monaco is bundled with Peacock and loaded when the first editor appears; nothing comes from a CDN, so it works under a content security policy that allows only its own origin. The code shows as plain text until Monaco is ready.
 - Its colors come from the theme's color roles and the code highlighter's syntax colors, so light, dark, the system color scheme and custom themes all follow the tokens.
 - Supports TypeScript, JavaScript, JSON, HTML, CSS, SCSS and Markdown, with completions and errors for TypeScript, JavaScript and JSON; read-only mode, line numbers, line wrapping and a minimap.
 - `lib-source` adds TypeScript declarations for completions, such as the modules a script may import.
 - With `breakpoint-gutter`, a click in the gutter fires `breakpoint-toggle`; `breakpoints` and `current-line` draw the marks a debugger shows.
 - `markers` underline problems, such as where a run failed.
 - With `fill`, the editor drops its frame and takes the height of its container, as a pane of its own.
 - It is a form field: `label` shows above the editor (and names it for assistive technology), `helper-text` below it, `error` with `error-text` puts it in its error state, and `required` blocks form submission while it is empty, with the message shown below once the value is committed or the form is submitted.
 - `file-name` is the header title, such as `theme.css`.
 - Fires `input` with `{ value }` on each edit and `change` with `{ value }` when the editor loses focus after an edit.
 - `size` sets the size of the code text: `sm` or `md` (the default), as on `wc-code-highlighter`.

**Breaking in 3.x:** `change` used to fire as a plain `Event` on every edit; it now fires once when the edit is committed (on blur), and `input` fires on every edit. Listen for `input` to keep the old timing.

**Deprecated:** `label` without `file-name` still shows in the header, as before, and logs a warning; set `file-name` for the header (or `file-name=""` for none) and `label` becomes the field label above the editor. In 4.0 `label` is always the field label. `line-numbers="on"` and `line-numbers="off"` still work; `line-numbers` is now a boolean that is on by default, so use `line-numbers="false"` (or the `lineNumbers = false` property) to hide them.

label: Condition Builder
summary: A query builder for composing filter conditions from rules and nested groups joined by And/Or.
overview:
The condition builder is the root group of a query. It holds rules (wc-cb-rule) and bordered nested groups (wc-cb-group), each joined by a bracket with an And/Or pill.

  • Click the pill to switch a group between And and Or.
  • Drag a rule by its handle to reorder it or move it between groups.
  • Without a mouse, focus a rule's handle: ArrowUp and ArrowDown move it within its group, ArrowRight moves it into the group beside it and ArrowLeft out of its group. Each move is announced.
  • Removing, moving and switching are built in; adding rules and groups is up to you, since only you know what a new rule contains. Listen for add-rule and add-group, which nested groups fire too; detail.group is the group to add to.
  • disabled and readonly apply to every group and rule inside: the add, remove and drag controls are hidden and the operator is locked. Disable or lock the slotted controls yourself.

value (read-only) returns the query as a tree, ready for JSON.stringify():

{
  type: 'group', id, operator: 'and' | 'or', data,
  children: [
    { type: 'rule', id, value, data },
    { type: 'group', id, operator, data, children: [...] }
  ]
}

id is the element's id, data its data-* attributes. A rule's value is the rule's own value property when set, else the values of the controls slotted into it: an object keyed by name when every control has a name, else an array. Each node also has a non-enumerable element, the element it came from, which JSON.stringify() leaves out.
fires: add-group - Dispatched when "Add inner group" is clicked, on this or a nested group.
slot: actions-end - Actions aligned to the end of the footer, such as a "Run query" button.
example:
```html
<wc-condition-builder operator="and">
  <wc-cb-rule>
    <wc-input placeholder="Value"></wc-input>
  </wc-cb-rule>
  <wc-cb-group operator="or">
    <wc-cb-rule>
      <wc-input placeholder="Value"></wc-input>
    </wc-cb-rule>
    <wc-cb-rule>
      <wc-input placeholder="Value"></wc-input>
    </wc-cb-rule>
  </wc-cb-group>
  <wc-button slot="actions-end">Run query</wc-button>
</wc-condition-builder>
```

label: Filter Bar
summary: The faceted filter row above a table or list: search, filter chips and saved views.
overview:
Describe the filters the person can use with filters, an array of { key, label, type, options?, placeholder? }. type picks the control the filter is edited with: select, multiselect, text, date-range or boolean (a switch).

"Add filter" opens a menu of the filters not in use yet. Each active filter is a dismissible chip, "Label: value"; a click (or Enter) on it opens its control in a popover, and its dismiss button (or Delete) removes it. "Clear all" removes every filter and keeps the search text.

value holds the active filters by key: a string for select and text, an array of strings for multiselect, start/end ISO dates for date-range and a boolean for boolean. With search, the search text is under the reserved key q. The value is plain JSON, so it can go in the URL. Every committed change fires change with { value }; typing in the search box fires input, and change once the text is committed (Enter, blur or clear).

Saved views: views lists named values, shown in a views menu with "All" (which clears the value). Picking one sets view to its id ('' for "All"), applies its value and fires view-change, then change. With saveable the menu has "Save view", which fires view-save with the current value; store it and add it to views. The views menu shows when there are views or saveable is set. view stays as it is when the person edits the filters afterwards.

Accessibility: the bar is a group named by label (default "Filters"). The chips are one tab stop: the arrow keys move between them (mirrored in right-to-left), Home and End jump to the ends. Each popover is a dialog named after its filter; Escape closes it and returns focus to the chip. Removing a filter is announced through a polite live region.
fires: view-save - Dispatched when the person picks "Save view".
example:
```html
<wc-filter-bar id="bar" search></wc-filter-bar>
<script>
  bar.filters = [
    { key: 'status', label: 'Status', type: 'select',
      options: [{ label: 'Open', value: 'open' }, { label: 'Closed', value: 'closed' }] },
    { key: 'archived', label: 'Archived', type: 'boolean' },
  ];
</script>
```

label: Select
summary: A dropdown select component supporting single and multi-select with optional typeahead search.
overview:
Select builds on wc-field and wc-menu to provide a fully-featured dropdown picker.

- Single and multi-select modes; a multi-select shows a checkbox on every option
- Client-side typeahead with `search="contains"`
- Server-side typeahead with `search="managed"`: listen to `search`, replace the options and set
  `loading` while they load; "No results" shows when the search leaves no option
- `allow-custom` keeps typed text that matches no option as the value, through a
  "Create …" row (or Enter in the search input) that fires `create`
- Multi-select chips on one row, with a "+N" chip for the ones that do not fit
- `clearable` adds a button that clears the value
- Form-associated: submits the value under `name` (one entry per value with `multiple`)
- Validates like a native select: `required` with nothing selected blocks form submission, and
  the message shows under the field once a value is committed or the form is submitted
- The options open in the top layer, so a select works inside a wc-modal

Options come from `<wc-option>` children or from the `options` property; use one or the other.
When both are given, both are shown: the options built from `options` follow the children, and
for a value present in both, the child (first in order) gives the label.

Keyboard: Enter, Space, Arrow Down or Arrow Up open the options and focus the selected one.
While closed, typing a letter selects the next option starting with it and Home or End select
the first or last option (single select, like a native select). In the list, the arrows move,
typing a letter jumps to the next option starting with it, Enter or Space picks, Escape closes
and returns focus to the field. With `search`, typing goes to the search input; Arrow Down moves
into the list and Enter picks the first match (with `allow-custom`, the typed text unless an
option's label matches it exactly).
slot: end - Trailing content, before the dropdown arrow.

example:

```html
  <wc-option value="apple">Apple</wc-option>
  <wc-option value="banana">Banana</wc-option>
</wc-select>
```

summary: Side sheets slide in from the start or end edge of the screen to reveal supplemental content. Supports standard and modal variants.
overview:

summary: Snackbars show brief, transient messages about app processes at the bottom of the screen.
overview:
An open snackbar is shown as a manual popover, so it renders in the browser's top layer, above sticky headers, app bars and open modals whatever their z-index. label: Tab Group
summary: The tab group component is used to display multiple panels of content in a container.
overview:
The tab group component allows users to switch between different views or content sections.

Tabs and panels are matched by value (<wc-tab value="billing"> shows <wc-tab-panel value="billing">), or by position when no tab has a value. Matching by the tab's target is deprecated and will be removed in 4.0; a link tab's target is always a link target.

The group wires the tabs pattern: each panel is labelled by its tab, and each tab points at its panel. Tabs and panels added later are wired too. When the wc-tabs is managed, the group leaves the selection to the consumer.

label: Table
summary: A configurable component for displaying tabular data.
overview:
The table displays rows of data with sorting (also by several columns), row selection, a sticky header, sticky start or end columns, and columns the user can resize, reorder and hide.

Put a wc-pagination in the footer slot to page the rows. When rows are selected, a bar over the header shows the count and the actions placed in the bulk-actions slot.

Rows can expand into a detail row (detailTemplate), be grouped under collapsible headers (group-by), and be edited in place (editable columns). Columns can show a footer aggregate (aggregate). virtual renders only the rows in view, for large data sets, and exportCsv() returns the rows as CSV.

label: Tabs

overview:
Tabs holds the tab buttons and manages their layout. It follows the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern: the host has role="tablist" (give it an aria-label), only the selected tab is a tab stop, and the Left and Right arrow keys (mirrored in right-to-left layouts), Home and End move between tabs. With managed, the tabs do not change the selection themselves: they fire change and the consumer sets selected on the chosen tab.

When every tab is a link (href), the tabs are navigation rather than a tablist: the host gets no tablist role, so wrap it in a <nav>.

summary: A group of related actions, such as editor formatting controls.
overview:
The toolbar groups related actions into one control. The floating variant (default) is an elevated pill that sits over content, such as a canvas or a selection. Render actions directly as children. Use a wc-divider to separate groups of actions; in a horizontal toolbar give it orientation="vertical".

The toolbar follows the WAI-ARIA toolbar pattern: it is a single tab stop, and the arrow keys along its orientation move focus between actions (Home and End jump to the first and last). Disabled actions and dividers are skipped. Give the toolbar an aria-label.

```html
  <wc-icon-button variant="text" color="surface" aria-label="Delete"><wc-icon name="delete"></wc-icon></wc-icon-button>
</wc-toolbar>
```
